newsitem.title: NORWAY: Hafslund 1996 pre-tax slips on financials.
newsitem.headline: Hafslund 1996 pre-tax slips on financials.

text.p: Norwegian power producer Hafslund ASA said on Wednesday operating profits in 1996 rose more than three percent although its result before tax was four percent lower due to a higher net financial item.
The energy group, which demerged from drug company Nycomed ASA in 1996, posted full-year operating profits of 274 million crowns against 265 million crowns in the corresponding 1995 period.
Pre-tax profits were 327 million crowns against 341 million crowns due to a increase of 21 million crowns in net financial charges because of lower realised profits on equities, Hafslund said.

"The increase in operating profit is mainly caused by the purchase of 28 percent of Fellesanlegget Kykkelsrud-Fossumfoss (FKF) power plant, and also higher water level than normal in the Glomma river in the fourth quarter 1996," it said in a statement.
Earnings per share for the 12-month period were 2.34 crowns compared with 2.44 crowns in 1995. The proposed dividend for the year was one crown per share.

For the fourth quarter, the company booked operating profits up more than 60 percent from a year-ago at 97 million crowns from 60 million crowns, which it attributed to additional production from the FKF acquisition.

Hafslund said it had bought during the fourth quarter a 45 percent stake in AS Oppdal Elektristetsverk. 28 percent of Arendal Fossekompani ASA, 25 percent in Drammen Kraftomsetning AS and 10 percent in Tussa Kraft AS.
In January 1997 it also acquired 100 percent of SkanKraft Holding AS.
Hafslund said spot electricity prices were high throughout the year due to low snow accumulation and low water levels in the country's hydropower reservoirs.
The average spot price in 1996 was 25.7 oere per kilowatt hour (kWh) compared with 11.9 oere/kWh a year earlier.
"As a result of better water accumulation and relatively high accumulation of snow, the price has dropped to around 15 oere/kWh on February 11," the company said.
